nodes.label: Life-cycle assessment of building materials

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Green buildings|Life-cycle assessment of building materials_qna_000
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: What is the main focus of the studies conducted by Cascione et al. (2022a, b) and Carcassi et al. (2022)?
nodes.answer: The main focus is on greenhouse emissions related to insulation manufacturing, particularly using bamboo and mycelium products.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Green buildings|Life-cycle assessment of building materials_qna_001
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What unique method did Carcassi et al. (2022) implement in their study?
nodes.answer: They implemented a dynamic life cycle impact assessment (LCIA) that accounts for the growth and cultivation of bamboo in insulation manufacturing.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Green buildings|Life-cycle assessment of building materials_qna_002
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: How did Schmidt et al. (2004a, b) and Schulte et al. (2021) evaluate bio-based insulation materials?
nodes.answer: They conducted a cradle-to-grave life cycle assessment (LCA) and compared the materials using thermal resistance as the functional unit while investigating all environmental impacts as prescribed in International Organization for Standardization (1997).

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Green buildings|Life-cycle assessment of building materials_qna_003
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What approach did Murphy and Norton (2008) use in their investigation of environmental impacts?
nodes.answer: Murphy and Norton (2008) used a cradle-to-grave approach to investigate the environmental impacts of natural fibre insulation materials.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Green buildings|Life-cycle assessment of building materials_qna_004
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What approach did Cascione et al. (2022a, b) take to analyze the lifecycle impacts of bio-based materials?
nodes.answer: Cascione et al. introduced a scenario-based Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) that considers variations in material properties, transportation scenarios, and end-of-life scenarios instead of providing single point-value results.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Green buildings|Life-cycle assessment of building materials_qna_005
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: How many newly commercially available bio-based insulation materials were included in the Life Cycle Assessment (LCA)?
nodes.answer: The LCA considered eleven newly commercially available bio-based insulation materials.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Green buildings|Life-cycle assessment of building materials_qna_006
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: From where was data collected to build Life Cycle Inventories (LCIs) for the studied materials?
nodes.answer: Data was collected from 603 articles published in The International Journal of Life Cycle Assessment to build the LCIs for the studied materials.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Green buildings|Life-cycle assessment of building materials_qna_007
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What was the outcome of the developed scenarios and dynamic LCIA in the project?
nodes.answer: The scenarios and dynamic LCIA provided a range of data for each environmental impact and material, helping professionals make informed design decisions.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Green buildings|Life-cycle assessment of building materials_qna_008
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What is the significance of using the LCA perspective in the study?
nodes.answer: The LCA (Life Cycle Assessment) perspective serves as the backbone for making recommendations regarding the evaluation of environmental impacts of EHDs.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Green buildings|Life-cycle assessment of building materials_qna_009
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: What methodology is used to evaluate the environmental impact of the biocomposite?
nodes.answer: A life cycle assessment (LCA) based on ISO 14040 and ISO 14044 is used to evaluate the environmental impact.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Green buildings|Life-cycle assessment of building materials_qna_010
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: Why is up-to-date data important for conducting Life Cycle Assessment (LCA)?
nodes.answer: Up-to-date data is crucial for conducting LCA as it reflects real changes in the environmental impacts of industrial activities over time.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Green buildings|Life-cycle assessment of building materials_qna_011
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: What does LCA guarantee in terms of evaluation processes?
nodes.answer: LCA guarantees rigor and uniformity in calculations, helping with the comparability of results and transparency in evaluation processes.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Green buildings|Life-cycle assessment of building materials_qna_012
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What methodology was applied in the construction industry to increase circularity?
nodes.answer: The Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) methodology was applied in the construction industry to increase circularity.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Green buildings|Life-cycle assessment of building materials_qna_013
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: What role do data protection and privacy concerns play in LCA?
nodes.answer: They may limit the effective sharing and use of information necessary for a complete and accurate life cycle assessment (LCA).

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Green buildings|Life-cycle assessment of building materials_qna_014
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What systematic approach is recommended in the literature review of life cycle assessment of buildings?
nodes.answer: The systematic approach recommended in the literature review involves conducting a comprehensive life cycle assessment of buildings to evaluate their environmental impact across all stages, from construction to demolition.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Green buildings|Life-cycle assessment of building materials_qna_015
nodes.label: Science and Tech
nodes.question: How has LCA been used to analyse the environmental impact of textile waste management solutions in the supply chain?
nodes.answer: LCA has been utilized in the strategy-planning process to examine the environmental effect of textile waste management solutions at various stages of the supply chain.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Green buildings|Life-cycle assessment of building materials_qna_016
nodes.label: Taxonomy
nodes.question: What are the core phases of Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) according to ISO standards?
nodes.answer: The core phases of LCA are Goal and Scope Definition, Inventory Analysis (LCD), Impact Assessment (CIA), and Interpretation.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Green buildings|Life-cycle assessment of building materials_qna_017
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How does the company use LCA to evaluate the environmental impact of garment production?
nodes.answer: The company uses LCA to assess each phase of production, from raw material acquisition to product distribution, focusing on KPIs like water use reduction and material recycling.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Green buildings|Life-cycle assessment of building materials_qna_018
nodes.label: Science and Tech
nodes.question: What is the approach used by GonzaloÃ‚Â¡lez, Lou, and Chi in 2023 to evaluate the environmental impact of fibres?
nodes.answer: GonzaloÃ‚Â¡lez, Lou, and Chi in 2023 used a Life cycle assessment approach to evaluate the environmental impact of natural and synthetic fibres.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Green buildings|Life-cycle assessment of building materials_qna_019
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What recommendation is made for improving impact assessment estimates in LCA studies?
nodes.answer: LCA studies should uniformly include SOC changes and be conducted over longer timespans to fully assess the stability of added C storage.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Green buildings|Life-cycle assessment of building materials_qna_020
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What are the two computational stages of LCA where uncertainties in carbon footprint estimates can arise?
nodes.answer: The two computational stages are life cycle inventory analysis (LCI) and life cycle impact assessment (LCIA).
